correctness.rationale: Every p-dividing-a term is a unit because the companion matrix fixes (1,1) mod p. In the regular case exact binomial divisibility leaves one unit leading term, proving an isometry for each parity and hence complete two-per-residue frequencies and least period. For p=2, h=1, a fourth-step matrix B has B²=0 mod2 and two selected 8-scaled isometric branches; their balls and an independent 3 mod8 term yield all four quotient unit balls. The 470 direct finite checks are corroboration, not the universal proof. Limits: primes not dividing a and the unclaimed complete exceptional value histogram.

value.rationale: The study addresses a mathematically motivated gap left by a published all-unit-seed non-density theorem: determining the exact quotient closure rather than just its non-density. A uniform prime-power isometry gives the full residue-fiber distribution and sharp scalar period in every regular case, and an exceptional two-adic lifting mechanism yields all units at the dyadic boundary. This distinguishes two genuinely different local dynamical regimes and may guide analogous recurrence quotient closures.
